brightness.name: Brightness
brightness.help:
Changes the brightness of the image using one of 3 different modes:
* **Adjust Gamma** - Similar to a camera's exposure setting.
* **Black/White Shift** - Moves all colors towards pure black or white.
* **Adjust Luminance** - Changes the perceptual lightness value in the Oklab color space.

The **Range** setting adjusts which light or dark values are affected, and the **Feather** setting works in combination with the **Range** to smooth out the transition.

chroma.name: Chroma
chroma.help:
Changes how colorful the image is, similar to "saturation" in some contexts.

* **Adjust Chroma Contrast** - Pixels that are already a higher chroma are affected more than lower chroma pixels.
* **Evenly Adjust Chroma** - The chroma levels of all pixels are adjusted with the same amount.

colorBlindness.name: Color Blindness
colorBlindness.help:
Simulates what the image would look like to a color blind person.

* **Brettel 1997** - More accurate simulation overall.
* **Viénot 1999** - A simpler simulation that in some studies participants have preferred it for protanopia and deuteranopia.

**Severity** adjusts how much the color blindness affects the image. Most color blind people are not 100% color blind, and sit somewhere in between.

contrast.name: Contrast
contrast.help:
Makes bright and dark values either closer to or farther apart from each other, adjusted in perceptual color space.

* **Contrast** - Higher increases value separation, lower decreases.
* **Middle Gray** - Adjust the gray point around which contrast is calculated.

cylinderBend.name: Cylinder Bend
cylinderBend.help:
Wraps the image around a 3D cylinder. Useful for scenarios like attaching paper signs to poles, etc.

* **Rotation** - Rotates the cylinder around the x-axis. This can be combined with the layer's z-axis rotation to achieve any display angle.
* **Perspective** - 0% is viewed from an infinite distance and 100% is very close.
* **View Position** - Shifts the view point up or down, which changes the perspective.

emboss.name: Emboss
emboss.help:
Simulates the 3D appearance of physical embossing, such as pressing a design into paper or metal.

* **Angle** - Controls the direction of the light and shadow.
* **Elevation** - Rases the height of the embossed area, increasing the strength of lights and shadows.

filmGrain.name: Film Grain
filmGrain.help:
Simulates the look of underexposed film or zoomed in film with large grain sizes.

* **Intensity** - Increases the visibility of the grain.
* **Grain Scale** - Increases grain size relative to pixel size.
* **Seed** - The random number used to generate the grain pattern.
* **Blend Mode** - Determines how the grain is merged with the image. Normal mode is physically correct, the other modes are for artistic effect.

gradientMap.name: Gradient Map
gradientMap.help:
Swaps out all colors in the image with colors from a gradient you specify, based on the brightness of the original colors in the image.

The **Color Space** changes how intermediate values between the stops on the gradient are interpolated. **Oklab** is generally the most accurate option.

grayscale.name: Grayscale
grayscale.help: Removes all color from the image, using one of many different formulas to calculate the brightness of the original colors.

modeOptionDescription.luminance: = (0.22 × R) + (0.72 × G) + (0.06 × B) as linearized RGB
modeOptionDescription.luma: = (0.22 × R) + (0.72 × G) + (0.06 × B) as non-linearized RGB

hue.name: Hue
hue.help:
Rotates the hue of colors in the image, effectively changing the perceived color.

The **Color Space** is used to determine the brightness and saturation of the new color. **Oklab** is generally the most accurate option.

The **Target Color** can be used to selectively modify only one specific color in the image. The **Range** determines what colors similar to the **Target Color** are affected.

monteCarloBlur.name: Monte Carlo Blur
monteCarloBlur.help:
Simulates the type of noisy blur you would see when taking a photograph in low light with a real camera.

* **Iterations** - How many rays of light are computed per pixel.
* **Size** - The radius of the blur.

negative.name: Negative
negative.help:
Invert specific color channels in the image, where high values become low values and vice versa.

The **Color Space** determines whether the invert occurs before or after gamma correction.

pixelize.name: Pixelize
pixelize.help: Covers up image detail with large squares that look like a pixel grid.

spread.name: Spread
spread.help: Shifts the pixels horizontally or vertically in a random noise pattern.

tiltShiftBlur.name: Tilt Shift Blur
tiltShiftBlur.help:
Simulates the effect of shallow depth of field at microscopic scales or a specialized camera tilt-shift lens.

* **Blur Radius** - The maximum amount of blur applied to the blurred areas.
* **Gradient Radius** - The size of the gradient from unblurred to blurred areas.
* **Angle** - The rotation of the unblurred area.
* **Offset** - The position of the unblurred area, offset from the center.

whirlPinch.name: Whirl & Pinch
whirlPinch.help:
Twists & pinches a circular area of the image.

* **Whirl** - The rotation of the twist.
* **Pinch** - The strength of pinching or expanding.
* **Radius** - The radius of the circle which determines the affected area.

whiteBalance.name: White Balance
whiteBalance.help:
Adjust the image as if the specified **Neutral Color** is actually supposed to be white.

Cameras can shift colors towards teal or orange depending on the lighting conditions, not matching what you actually see in real life.

zoomBlur.name: Zoom Blur
zoomBlur.help:
Simulates the blur from a photographic technique called a **zoom burst**.

Higher **Strength** gives stronger blur, representing a slower shutter speed or longer exposure.

createCircleShape.description: Adds a SVG <circle> shape to the current selected layer, or to a new layer if the current selected layer isn't a vector layer. The new shape is drawn on top of all other shapes in the layer.

property.cx: The the x position of the circle's center in pixels.
property.cy: The the y position of the circle's center in pixels.
property.r: The radius of the circle pixels.

createEllipseShape.description: Adds a SVG <ellipse> shape to the current selected layer, or to a new layer if the current selected layer isn't a vector layer. The new shape is drawn on top of all other shapes in the layer.

property.cx: The the x position of the ellipse's center in pixels.
property.cy: The the y position of the ellipse's center in pixels.
property.rx: The radius of the ellipse along the x axis in pixels.
property.ry: The radius of the ellipse along the y axis in pixels.

createLineShape.description: Adds a SVG <line> shape to the current selected layer, or to a new layer if the current selected layer isn't a vector layer. The new shape is drawn on top of all other shapes in the layer.

property.x1: The the x position of the start of the line in pixels.
property.y1: The the y position of the start of the line in pixels.
property.x2: The the x position of the end of the line in pixels.
property.y2: The the y position of the end of the line in pixels.

createPathShape.description: Adds a SVG <path> shape to the current selected layer, or to a new layer if the current selected layer isn't a vector layer. The new shape is drawn on top of all other shapes in the layer.

property.d: The list of SVG path commands. Follow the SVG spec. Example: "M 10 80 Q 52.5 10, 95 80 T 180 80"

createPolygonShape.description: Adds a SVG <polygon> shape to the current selected layer, or to a new layer if the current selected layer isn't a vector layer. The new shape is drawn on top of all other shapes in the layer.

property.points: The points which define the outer edge of the shape. Example: "0,0 20,0 10,5"

createPolylineShape.description: Adds a SVG <polyline> shape to the current selected layer, or to a new layer if the current selected layer isn't a vector layer. The new shape is drawn on top of all other shapes in the layer.

property.points: The points which define the connected lines. Example: "0,0 20,0 10,5"

createRectangleShape.description: Adds a SVG <rect> shape to the current selected layer, or to a new layer if the current selected layer isn't a vector layer. The new shape is drawn on top of all other shapes in the layer.

property.x: The the x position of the rectangle's left edge in pixels.
property.y: The the y position of the rectangle's left edge in pixels.
property.rx: The x radius of the rectangle's corners in pixels.
property.ry: The y radius of the rectangle's corners in pixels.
property.width: The width of the rectangle in pixels.
property.height: The height of the rectangle in pixels.

property.fill: The fill color as a RGB 8-bit per channel hex. Omit for no fill. Example: "#000000"
property.fillOpacity: The opacity of the fill color as a decimal number from 0 to 1.
property.stroke: The stroke color as a RGB 8-bit per channel hex. Omit for no stroke. Example: "#000000"
property.strokeLinecap: How the ends of lines are rendered, as defined in the SVG spec.
property.strokeLinejoin: How the corners of joined lines are rendered, as defined in the SVG spec.
property.strokeOpacity: The opacity of the stroke color as a decimal number from 0 to 1.
property.strokeWidth: The width of the stroke in pixels.
property.transform: The transform attribute on the shape. Must be a SVG 2D matrix transform function. Example: "matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)"

error.fill: Invalid fill syntax. Provide a RGBA 8-bit per channel hex. Example: "#000000"
error.stroke: Invalid stroke syntax. Provide a RGBA 8-bit per channel hex. Example: "#000000"
error.transform: Invalid transform syntax. Provide a SVG 2D matrix transform function. Example: "matrix(1,0,0,1,0,0)"

cropWorkingFile.description: Crops the entire image canvas in the working file (all layers). A negative crop can be used to increase the canvas size.

property.left: The left-most boundary of the cropped image in pixels. This can be negative.
property.top: The top-most boundary of the cropped image in pixels. This can be negative.
property.width: The new width of the cropped image in pixels. This can be larger than the original width.
property.height: The new height of the cropped image in pixels. This can be larger than the original height.

getEditorGuide.description: Provides a natural language summary of how the OpenGraphica image editor works.
getEditorGuide.summary:
OpenGraphica is a 2D mixed-media image editor. At its core, it can edit both raster images and vector shapes, and export to both raster and vector image formats.

The working file in OpenGraphica is a image document with one or more layers. It has a fixed rectangular resolution, defined in pixels. Other measuring units such as mm are supported in the UI for display purposes, but they are converted to pixels for editing by using the resolutionX and resolutionY settings. The working file image document has a coordinate system where +x is right, +y is down, and -z goes into the screen, away from the viewer.

The working file is composed of a stack of individual layers. All layers have a width/height defined in pixels, and a 3x3 2D transformation matrix which determines their position / rotation / scale. With an identity transformation matrix, a layer is drawn with its top-left corner aligned with the top-left of the working file.

Layers have different types, which infer the type of image they contain:
* **gradient** - A linear or radial gradient which covers the entirety of the working file.
**raster** - An 8-bit per channel RGBA pixel-based image.
* **rasterSequence** - An animation sequence using 8-bit per channel RGBA pixel-based images for each frame.
* **text** - One or more paragraphs of rich text drawn horizontally or vertically.
* **vector** - A SVG 1.x document.
* **video** - A video using a web-supported codec.

Layers are stacked from bottom to top, where the bottom layer is drawn first, and the top layer is drawn in front of all other layers. Layers are stored so that the first layer in the array is the bottom-most layer, but they are displayed to the end-user where the top-most layers list. Layers are composited by default with source over blending in linear RGB, and converted to sRGB after all compositing operations are completed.

getLayerList.description: Returns a JSON summary definition of all layers in the working file, where layers are drawn in array order (last on top).

getRasterLayerImage.description: Returns the image data for the specified raster layer.

property.id: The ID of the raster layer. This can be retrieved from the get-layer-list tool.

getShapeList.description: Returns a JSON definition that lists all shapes in any currently selected vector layers, in order from bottom to top. The shape IDs can change whenever a new shape is added, deleted, or reordered.

getVectorLayerSvg.description: Returns the serialized SVG document associated with the specified vector layer.

property.id: The ID of the vector layer. This can be retrieved from the get-layer-list tool.

insertRasterLayer.description: Inserts a 8-bit RGBA image as a new raster layer on the top of the layer stack.

property.imageDataUri: A base64 encoded image data URI. Media types image/png or image/jpeg are acceptable.
property.name: The name of the new layer; usually the filename of the image.
property.transform: An array of 6 numbers which represents the 2D transform matrix. Example identity transform: [1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1]

property.insertLayerIds: The IDs of layers to insert at the specified insertPosition in the layer stack. The layer IDs can be retrieved from the get-layer-list tool.
property.referenceLayerId: The ID of the layer to insert around, based on the insertPosition property.
property.insertPosition: The position to insert around the layer referenced by referenceLayerId. "above" or "below".

error.noInsertIds: Provide at least one ID in the insertLayerIds property

resampleWorkingFile.description: Resamples the entire image canvas in the working file (all layers) at a different resolution. Also known as scaling the image size.

property.width: The new width of the resampled image in pixels.
property.height: The new height of the resampled image in pixels. The aspect ratio of width to height must match the original image.

selectLayers.description: Sets which layers are currently selected in the editor by providing their IDs

property.ids: An array of layer IDs (number values)

error.noIds: You must provide at least one layer ID in the ids property.

setLayerTransform.description: Sets the currently selected layers' 3x3 2D transformation matrix which controls its position, rotation, and scale.

property.transform: An array of 6 numbers which represents the 2D transform matrix. Example identity transform: [1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1]

setShapeAttributes.description: Updates the SVG attributes of any vector shape in any currently selected vector layers: <rect>, <circle>, <ellipse>, <line>, <polyline>, <polygon>, or <path>.

property.id: The ID of the shape to update. This can be retrieved from the get-shape-list tool.
property.cx: The x position of the center of a circle or ellipse in pixels.
property.cy: The y position of the center of a circle or ellipse in pixels.
property.rx: The x radius of a rectangle's corners or an ellipse's radius in pixels.
property.ry: The y radius of a rectangle's corners or an ellipse's radius in pixels.
property.points: The points which define the outer edge of a polyline or polygon shape. Example: "0,0 20,0 10,5"

normal.description: The top layer covers the bottom based on its opacity.
normal.example: Cutting out a person from one photo and adding them to another photo.

dissolve.description: Randomly replaces pixels from the top layer with transparent pixels based on opacity, creating a digital noise effect.

colorErase.description: Removes the color from the top layer that matches the color of the lower layer.
colorErase.example: Removing a green screen background from an image.

erase.description: Erases the bottom layers where the top layer is opaque.
erase.example: Removing unwanted objects in a photo by erasing those areas.

merge.description: The top layer covers the bottom based on its opacity, but it merges transparent edges together when the opacity values can add up to be opaque. Merging only works on top of a transparent background.
merge.example: Cutting a selected area from a photo and pasting it in the same location on a new layer.

lightenOnly.description: Keeps the lighter color in each R,G,B channel of the top and bottom layers.
lightenOnly.example: Adding a glow effect to an object without darkening the surrounding areas.

lumaLightenOnly.description: Compares the perceptual brightness between the top and bottom layers and keeps the brighter pixels.
lumaLightenOnly.example: Enhancing the brightness of a specific area in a black and white photo.

screen.description: Lightens the bottom layer based on the brightness of the top layer. Screen mimics the way light interacts when projected or layered.
screen.example: Making a night scene appear brighter.

dodge.description: Significantly brightens highlights and brings out details in the shadows. This mimics the effect of "dodging" in darkroom photography.

linearDodge.description: Adds the brightness of the top and bottom layers in perceptual SRGB space.

addition.description: Adds the brightness of the top and bottom layers in linear SRGB space.

darkenOnly.description: Keeps the darker color in each R,G,B channel of the top and bottom layers.
darkenOnly.example: Darkening the shadows in a photo.

lumaDarkenOnly.description: Compares the perceptual darkness between the top and bottom layers and keeps the darker pixels.

multiply.description: Darkens the bottom layer based on the darkness of the top layer. Multiply mimics how multiple photographic negatives look when layered together.
multiply.example: Making an image look darker, like simulating shadows or night scenes.

burn.description: Darkens the bottom layer proportional to the darkness of the top layer.

linearBurn.description: Adds the pixels of the upper and lower layers, then subtracts the brightest possible value.
linearBurn.example: Adding a dramatic shadowy look to the image.

overlay.description: A combination of multiply and screen, where light areas become lighter and dark areas become darker.
overlay.example: Adding contrast to photos without losing detail.

softLight.description: Brightens the image similar to overlay but with more gradual transitions. Soft light simulates diffused lighting.
softLight.example: Adding a soft glow to portraits.

hardLight.description: A harsher version of overlay, where bright areas become much brighter and dark areas much darker.
hardLight.example: Dramatically increasing the contrast in action scenes.

vividLight.description: Increases the contrast very strongly, even more compared to hard light.
vividLight.example: Stylizing photos with bold, punchy colors and contrast.

pinLight.description: Replaces pixels based on brightness, keeping the brightest and darkest pixels, based on their distance from midtones.
pinLight.example: Creating a posterized effect with sharp contrast between light and dark.

linearLight.description: Increases contrast linearly, brightening or darkening based on the top layer.
linearLight.example: Simulating artificial lighting or enhancing metallic surfaces.

hardMix.description: Reduces the image to primary colors, creating a highly stylized look.
hardMix.example: Creating a comic book or screen-printed effect.

difference.description: Finds the difference between layers, where black is no difference increasing color brightness is more different.
difference.example: Aligning layers with similar content. When two pixels are the same, they turn black.

exclusion.description: A variation of difference with less contrast, for where subtle differences need to be highlighted without overwhelming the image.

subtract.description: Subtracts the brightness in the top layer from the bottom. The result is a lot of black or near-black areas.

grainExtract.description: Extracts the film grain from a layer, also gives an embossed appearance.
grainExtract.example: Extracting grain from a film texture to apply to another texture.

grainMerge.description: Adds grain from the top layer to the bottom, leaving a grainy version of the original layer.
grainMerge.example: Adding film grain to a digital image for a vintage look.

divide.description: Divides the brightness of the top layer by the bottom.
divide.example: Lighting up an image dramatically, creating a glowing or ethereal effect. Can be used for exposure correction.

hue.description: Uses the hue of the top layer while preserving the chroma and lightness of the bottom layer.
hue.example: Changing a blue sky to purple while retaining its brightness.

chroma.description: Uses the chroma (intensity of color) of the top layer while preserving the hue and lightness of the bottom layer.
chroma.example: Boosting or reducing the intensity of colors in a photo.

color.description: Combines the hue and chroma of the top layer with the lightness of the bottom layer.
color.example: Recoloring an object while keeping the shading and lighting intact.

lightness.description: Uses the lightness of the top layer while preserving the hue and chroma of the bottom layer.
lightness.example: Lighting or darkening an image while keeping the original colors.

luminance.description: Divides upper layer luminance by lower layer, then multiplies the result to the lower layer.
luminance.example: Lighting or darkening an image while keeping the original colors.

blending.densityDescription: How transparent each stamp of the brush will be, based on pen pressure. The range is used when varying pen pressure.
blending.colorBlendingStrengthDescription: How much of the color underneath the brush will be picked up while drawing. The range is used when varying pen pressure.
blending.colorBlendingPersistenceDescription: How long the picked up color remains on the brush while dragging the stroke.
blending.concentrationDescription: Lower values simulate brush dilution with water, and high values full concentrated color. This setting has no effect when drawing on top of fully opaque colors. The range is used when varying pen pressure.

shape.title: Shape
shape.hardnessDescription: Lower values will have soft faded edges, and higher values sharp edges.

strokePath.title: Stroke Path
strokePath.spacingDescription: The distance between each stamp of the brush, relative to the brush size. Be careful with extremely low values, as it can tank performance on larger brush sizes.
strokePath.jitterDescription: Randomly shifts the position of the brush shape.

pressure.title: Pressure
pressure.pressureTaperDescription: Higher values will draw skinnier lines at lower pen pressures. Makes it easier to control pens with unstable sensitivity at lower pressures.
pressure.pressureMinSizeDescription: The size of the brush at 0% pen pressure, relative to the currently selected brush size.

invisibleShape.title: Creating Invisible Shape
invisibleShape.message: Both your current fill and stroke color are fully transparent. A new shape will not be created.

invisibleLine.title: Creating Invisible Line
invisibleLine.message: The current stroke color must not be fully transparent, and the stroke width must be greater than 0.

message.touch: Touch and drag your finger on an empty area to add new shapes.
message.mouse: Click and drag on an empty area to add new shapes.

edit.noLayersSelected: Please select one or more layers in the layers dock in order to edit their effects.

noSelectedLayers.title: No Layers Selected
noSelectedLayers.message: Please select at least one image layer in the layers dock. Certain layer types can't be erased.

noSelectedLayers.title: No Layers Selected
noSelectedLayers.message: Please select at least one image layer in the layers dock. Certain layer types can't be erased.

unproductiveSelection.message:

Please select at least one image layer in the layers dock.

deform.description: Tools that manipulate the existing image data, such as cloning, bulging, blurring.

blur.name: Blur
blur.description: Brush that blurs the area drawn.

draw.name: Draw
draw.description: Brushes, pencils, pens, and vector art drawing tools.

brush.name: Brush
brush.description: Draw on layers as if you are using a paint brush.

bucketFill.name: Bucket Fill
bucketFill.description: Fill in areas of similar color.

effect.name: Effect
effect.description: Adjust layer colors, add blurring and other effects.

cropResize.name: Crop and Resize
cropResize.description: Crop, resize, change aspect ratio, or resample the image.

selection.name: Selection
selection.description: Select areas of the active layer(s), any manipulations to the layer(s) only occur inside the selection.

selection.name: Selection
selection.description: Select an area of the image for targeted editing.

transform.name: Transform
transform.description: Tools for moving, rotating, scaling the layer.

freeTransform.name: Free Transform
freeTransform.description: Move, rotate, or scale the selected layers.

view.name: Viewport Display
view.description: Tools for controlling the viewport display of the canvas.

tools.name: Zoom
tools.description: Zoom in and out the canvas to control how much of the image you can see.

cloneBrushToolIntroduction.title: Clone Brush Tool
introduction: The clone brush copies part of an image so you can paint that same area somewhere else. It is typically used to remove blemishes, unwanted objects, or fill in a damaged spot.

mouse: The clone area displays as a circle with the clone stamp icon. You can drag it around or ctrl + click to set it to the current mouse position.
touch: The clone area displays as a circle with the clone stamp icon. You can drag it around.

deformBlurToolIntroduction.title: Blur Tool
introduction: The blur tool will blur the portion of current layer you draw on.

deformSharpenToolIntroduction.title: Sharpen Tool
introduction: The sharpen tool will sharpen areas of the current layer you draw on.

drawBrushToolIntroduction.title: Brush Tool
introduction: The brush tool lets you create a painting with different brushes. It is best used with a pressure-sensitive stylus.

drawBucketFillToolIntroduction.title: Bucket Fill Tool
introduction: The bucket fill tool lets you fill in areas of similar color with a color of your choice.

mouse: Click on an area to fill. While holding the mouse down, you can drag to the left or right to adjust how much of the area is filled.
touch: Tap on an area to fill. While holding down, you can drag to the left or right to adjust how much of the area is filled.

drawGradientToolIntroduction.title: Gradient Tool
introduction: The gradient tool lets you add gradient layers.

mouse: Click and drag to place a gradient on the canvas.
touch: Use one finger to touch and drag to place a gradient on the canvas.

drawShapeToolIntroduction.title: Shape Tool
introduction: The shape tool lets you add various basic shapes and vector paths.

mouse: {add} - Click and drag to place a shape on the canvas.
{edit} - Click on a shape's control points and drag them to edit the shape after it has been added.
touch: {add} - Use one finger to touch and drag to place a shape on the canvas.
{edit} - Tap a shape's control points and drag them to edit the shape after it has been added.

effectToolIntroduction.title: Effect Tool
introduction: The effect tool allows to add layer effects that can adjust colors and do all sorts of other useful operations to the entire layer. Effects can be stacked and removed at any time.

eraseBucketFillToolIntroduction.title: Erase Bucket Fill Tool
introduction: Erase areas of the image that have a similar color.

mouse: Click on an area to erase. While holding the mouse down, you can drag to the left or right to adjust how much of the area is erased.
touch: Tap on an area to erase. While holding down, you can drag to the left or right to adjust how much of the area is erased.

eraseToolIntroduction.title: Erase Tool
introduction: The erase tool allows you to remove parts of the layer, making them transparent.

explainCanvasViewportControls.title: Moving the Canvas
introduction: No matter which tool is selected, you can control the canvas view.

mouse: {zooming} - Use the {mouseWheel} to zoom in and out.
{panning} - Click and drag with the {rightMouseButton} to move the canvas.
touch: {zooming} - Use two fingers and pinch to zoom in and out.
{panning} - Use two fingers and slide them together to move the canvas.

freeTransformToolIntroduction.title: Free Transform Tool
introduction: This tool moves, resizes, and rotates layers. A boundary box shows around the selected layer(s).

mouse: {selection} - {leftClick} on a layer to select it.
{moving} - {leftClick} on a layer and drag to move it.
touch: {selection} - Tap on a layer to select it.
{moving} - Tap on a layer and drag to move it.
{resizing} - Use one finger to drag resize handles.

selectionToolIntroduction.title: Selection Tool
introduction: The selection tool allows you to select specific parts of the image to restrict what editing affects.

mouse: {createSelection} - Click and drag with {leftClick} to create a selection.
touch: {createSelection} - Draw with one finger to create a selection.
end: {selectionShape} - What shape is used to draw the selection.
{selectionCombineMode} - How the current selection combines with the existing selection.

zoomToolIntroduction.title: Zoom/Pan Tool
introduction: This tool lets you zoom in to the image, and move the view around.

mouse: {zooming} - {leftClick} to zoom in; {ctrlLeftClick} to zoom out.
{panning} - Click and drag with the {leftMouseButton} to move the canvas.
touch: {zooming} - Tap with one finger to zoom in. Tap with two fingers to zoom out.
{panning} - Tap and drag with one finger to move the canvas.
